page: Amazon Web Services i4i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and third-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores with two threads per core. Hardware specifications include 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, 15,000 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps. Cryptographic execution is supported through hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA-NI extensions, alongside vector extensions including AVX-512.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong multi-threaded compute and data transaction performance. The instance achieves top-quartile results in PassMark database operations with a score of 26,317.04, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 57,600.73 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 61,946.14. High concurrent throughput is further indicated by static web serving speeds reaching 45.18 GB/sec and strong software compilation marks in Clang tests. In contrast, single-core evaluations such as Geekbench single-core at 1,688.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1,893.69 perform within the middle 50 percent bracket.

The combination of 15,000 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage and 512 GB of memory offers high resource density for workloads constrained by disk throughput and low-latency access requirements. While it lacks hardware GPU accelerators for specialized machine learning training, its large local storage capacity eliminates the latency and network dependency of external volumes. The i4i.16xlarge is best suited for I/O-intensive transactional databases, NoSQL stores, search indexes, distributed cache platforms, and high-volume data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 512 GB of DDR4 memory, and 15,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, supported by a 38 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute and database operations, registering 26,317.04 in PassMark database tests and 45.18 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-core processing and cached memory bandwidth track within median parameters. The dense integration of local flash storage and an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation minimizes network I/O bottlenecks without external volumes. This configuration is engineered for high-transaction databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed data analytics, and search indexing.
